description_long: An internal draft alleges that Donald Trump made 11 trips on Jeffrey Epstein's aircraft between April 1993 and July 1998, mainly between Palm Beach and the New York area. It says Ghislaine Maxwell was on seven of the flights and lists Mark Epstein, Eva and Celina Dubin, and two other named passengers. Those details are retained only as supplied claims: the packet does not include the flight logs or an opened source that establishes the count, dates, routes, aircraft, or passenger identities. The alleged travel, even if documented, would not by itself establish knowledge of Epstein's crimes or misconduct by any passenger. Keep the record internal until the logs or a verifiable contemporaneous report can support a narrower account.

title: DOJ Drops Proposed Google AI-Investment Divestiture While Seeking Other Remedies
description_short: DOJ revised its Google search-case proposal on March 7, 2025, dropping mandatory AI-investment divestiture while retaining a proposed Chrome divestiture.
description_medium: On March 7, 2025, the Justice Department filed a revised proposed judgment in the Google search-monopoly case. The proposal dropped mandatory divestiture of Google's AI investments in favor of advance notice for future investments, while retaining a proposed Chrome divestiture and other remedies. Reuters reported that DOJ and 38 state attorneys general continued seeking court relief. This was a change in proposed remedies, not dismissal of the antitrust case or a final court order.
description_long: On March 7, 2025, the U.S. Department of Justice and plaintiff states filed a revised proposed final judgment in the federal search-monopoly case against Google. The filing changed the remedies sought: plaintiffs stopped seeking mandatory divestiture of Google's AI investments and instead proposed prior notification of future investments. It maintained other central requests, including Google's divestiture of Chrome, restrictions on search-related payments to distribution partners, and data-sharing provisions. Reuters reported that DOJ and a coalition of 38 state attorneys general still sought a court order requiring Chrome's sale and other measures. The filing was a proposal submitted for the court's consideration; it did not dismiss the antitrust case or establish a quid pro quo. The supplied record's claim that Attorney General Pam Bondi dropped the case after Alphabet made political contributions or held meetings with Donald Trump is not supported by the accessed sources and is excluded. The official filing says plaintiffs changed the AI remedy after additional discovery, but this alone does not prove the rationale or rule out other motives. This corrected entry is limited to the documented procedural change and the remedies still proposed at that point.
subcategory: Proposed remedies in the Google search case

As detailed further below, Plaintiffs no longer seek the mandatory divestiture of Google’s AI investments in favor of a prior notification for future investments.
